page: Amazon Web Services c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25 percent under stress-ng testing. Multi-core performance, software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations fall within the average tier. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25 percent. Similarly, while LLM inference speeds for small 135M models are average, prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak.

The instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power, though the DDR4 memory bandwidth limits performance on memory-intensive datasets. This server is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, single-threaded compression tasks, and moderate database operations.
